submissions.title: IREN Announces Successful Energization of Sweetwater 1
submissions.excerpt: successful energization of its 1.4GW Sweetwater 1 data center site in Texas
submissions.note: AUDIT: the tracker's HIGH-confidence 2,000 MW POWER_MW row is labeled 'Basis: IT load,' but its own methodology note in the same field explains energization is only the high-voltage substation connection to ERCOT ('Power delivery... expected to ramp progressively in line with phased construction and commissioning'), and the cited release itself describes 1.4GW of site/grid energization for Sweetwater 1 — no IT capacity is confirmed operating yet. The Basis label directly contradicts the row's own text. Recommend correcting Basis to site/grid interconnection power (aggregate target: Sweetwater 1 1.4GW + Sweetwater 2 0.6GW), not IT load, and not energized/operating capacity.

submissions.title: HUMAIN and NVIDIA Announce Strategic Partnership to Build AI Factories of the Future in Saudi Arabia
submissions.excerpt: a major investment to build AI factories in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia with a projected capacity of up to 500 megawatts
submissions.note: AUDIT: the tracker's HIGH-confidence 200 MW POWER_MW row cites this exact release as its source, but the release's own captured text states a program-wide 'projected capacity of up to 500 megawatts' — an aspirational target, not 200 MW, and not specific to the two launch sites. The tracker's own methodology text admits '200 MW... basis unstated' — no source in the record actually supports the 100MW-per-site/200MW-combined figure, so this is a citation mismatch (HIGH confidence resting on a source that doesn't state the claimed number). Recommend downgrading the 200 MW row's confidence until a source explicitly stating the 100MW-per-site figure is found, and recording the 500 MW program-wide figure separately, clearly labeled as an aspirational/projected target, not current or per-site capacity.

claims.methodology: Basis: unclear (program-wide, not per-site). Source explicitly frames this as a 'projected capacity' target for HUMAIN's NVIDIA-partnered buildout, not current or energized capacity.

submissions.title: SoftBank Group to Build 5 GW of AI Data Center Capacity in France
submissions.excerpt: initial €45 billion investment to deliver 3.1 GW of AI data center capacity
submissions.note: AUDIT: this project record is scoped to the three named Hauts-de-France sites (Loon-Plage/Dunkirk, Bosquel, Bouchain), but its headline power.estimatedMw=5000 and capex.estimatedUsd=$87B are SoftBank's national, up-to, conditional program ceiling, not the firm commitment to these sites. SoftBank's own release states the firm, region-specific figure is 3.1 GW for an initial €45B investment; scaling to 5GW/€75-87B is conditional on phase-1 success and may include sites beyond Hauts-de-France. The project's analystNotes already acknowledge the 3.1GW/€45B phase-1 split in prose, but the structured power/capex fields still carry the larger national-ceiling numbers as if they were this project's own figures. Recommend recording 3,100 MW / ~$48-49B (USD equivalent of €45B) as the primary figures for this project, keeping 5,000 MW/$87B only as a clearly-labeled national-program-ceiling reference, not this project's capacity.

claims.methodology: Basis: unclear (source says 'AI data center capacity,' not explicitly IT load or site power). Firm first-phase commitment per SoftBank's own press release, specific to the Hauts-de-France sites, targeted by 2031 — not yet under construction.

USD-equivalent of the stated firm €45 billion first-phase investment (approximate FX conversion); distinct from the conditional up-to-€75B/$87B national ceiling currently recorded as this project's capex.
